name: Sonnet concentrated AI/technology
strategy: Concentrated long book in AI infrastructure leaders (compute, networking, memory) with leveraged semis beta for extra torque, a modest single-name short to offset gross exposure, and cash held for weekly rebalancing flexibility.

positions.thesis: Core AI compute bottleneck confirmed by Aug 26 blowout print ($96.2B rev +106% YoY, FY28 growth guided to 70% vs 44% consensus, AWS committing to 2M GPUs). Stock only net +1.5% on the week despite the beat, suggesting it's already reflected in price -- holding current size, not chasing the print.

Strongest clean confirming trend in the book: +6.3% this week to $513.53 with no negative catalyst, on continued 43% Azure growth and 30M+ paid Copilot seats. Sizing up from 28% to 30%, funded by the MU trim rather than cash, since this is the highest-conviction, lowest-controversy leg right now.

Custom-silicon/networking diversification intact but facing a real new competitive catalyst: Marvell and Google's TPU/custom-chip commercial agreement hit shares -5% intraday this week, and Google qualifying MediaTek/AMD as alternate TPU sources is a genuine moat question, not noise. Holding the de-risked 10% into the Sept 2 earnings binary but tightening the stop to -15% given the incremental risk.

MI-series share-gain thesis confirmed a second straight week: Q3 revenue guide of $13.0B (41% YoY) beat the $12.5B Street consensus, stock +5% on Aug 26 to $479.18. Holding size unchanged -- two consecutive confirming catalysts already justified the prior size-up, no case to add further here.

HBM/memory structural-tightness thesis is now facing compounding negative, catalyst-grade information: a report that Apple may source memory from Chinese suppliers (ChangXin/YMTC) directly threatens the competitive-moat framing, plus a fresh patent-litigation overhang and Samsung's capital-return disappointment dragging sector sentiment. Stock -3.5% this week to $932.86, ~30% off its June high. Trimming from 6% to 4% and tightening the stop from -20% to -15% rather than holding unchanged into a third week of deteriorating news flow.

research_notes:
Checked point-in-time news/prices through 2026-08-28 close for every held name in both books.

Round 2 (AI/semis long book): NVDA reported Aug 26 -- revenue $96.2B (+106% YoY), EPS $2.22, FY28 growth guided to 70% vs 44% street, plus AWS committing to 2M Nvidia GPUs -- a clean beat-and-raise, but the stock is only net +1.5% for the week ($214.72->$217.89), so the print looks priced in already. MSFT is the standout: +6.3% to $513.53 on continued 43% Azure growth and 30M+ Copilot seats, no negative catalyst. AMD's Q3 guide ($13.0B, 41% YoY) beat the $12.5B Street consensus, stock +5% Aug 26 to $479.18, a second confirming week. AVGO took a real hit: Marvell+Google's TPU/custom-chip commercial agreement (Google also reportedly qualifying MediaTek/AMD as alternate TPU sources) knocked AVGO -5% intraday; earnings land Sept 2 so this is a genuine live risk, not settled. MU is the negative-catalyst leg: a report that Apple may source memory from Chinese suppliers (ChangXin/YMTC), a new patent-litigation overhang, and Samsung's capital-return disappointment dragging sector sentiment -- stock -3.5% this week to $932.86, ~30% off its June high.

Round 3 (cross-sector momentum book): XBI choppy/rangebound this week (roughly $162-169 vs last week's $165.73), 2026 biotech M&A run-rate ($106B/201 deals) still intact, no confirmed breakdown. KRE steady near $74.35 (vs $74.86), NIM-widening fundamental story still standing. TLT is the key finding: 30Y yields stabilized near 5.2% post Treasury-buyback announcement and TLT rose for a second straight week ($82.05->$83.12) -- exactly the risk flagged last week to the short -- and GDX, this book's other falling-yield short casualty (already stopped out), kept climbing too ($102.83->$103.64), confirming a broad falling-real-yield theme working against the short rather than a one-week blip. Bitcoin traded ~$79-80k, still well above the level that stopped out the IBIT short, so crypto-weakness remains unavailable as previously noted.
